scope: Read-only sample of position and adjacent normal records in running QuickSurface process
capture: After finding the first input vertex coordinate in writable process memory, 64 adjacent 48-byte records were sampled at XYZ offsets 0,4,8 and vector offsets 16,20,24. The code path previously inspected reads its three vectors at offset 0x10 from facet vertex pointers.
result: All 64 positions uniquely match the original imported input topology, and all 192 sampled vector components match independently computed ScanForge geometry normals bit-for-bit.
limitations: The scan discovered a memory block by coordinate match; ownership by the visible scene object or by an STL export invocation was not established. Multiple memory copies of the first vertex existed.
The contiguous 64 records are a sample, not all scan vertices or seam configurations.
No user interface action, native export, or mutation of target memory was performed. Native process memory changed by the application independently during inspection remains outside this observation.
The capture is of the earlier running process and may not be valid as an address after restart.

pointerSearchFollowup.scope: Read-only exact 64-bit little-endian pointer searches for two sampled first-vertex record addresses across writable process ranges.
pointerSearchFollowup.result: No exact pointer bytes were found for either allocation in the writable ranges scanned at those times.
limitations: This is a raw-byte search only; it does not cover read-only mappings, indirect representations, register values, or memory that changed during scanning.
The result does not prove these records are stale, and it does not connect either allocation to a scene object or writer invocation.

facetPointerFollowup.scope: A third matching allocation was found by scanning readable process memory for its pointer. Seven candidate records contain three such pointers; each references an ordered facet of the original scan.
facetPointerFollowup.result: All seven facet coordinate sequences uniquely match the original input; all 63 referenced normal components match ScanForge computed geometry normals exactly.
limitations: These are raw memory observations, not a captured export invocation or proof that the records are owned by the currently visible scene object.
Seven neighboring facets and one scan do not cover all vertices, seam cases, or formats.
The first two allocations had no references in the writable ranges scanned; this third allocation was found in readable ranges.
